turns.t: My stomach's been off since I started something new last month. I figured I should get it looked at.
Good call. I'll ask a few things first, then we'll take your vitals. Can you describe how it's been off?
Just off. Not great.
Okay. Is it there after you eat, in the morning, or at random?
Kind of random.
Alright. I won't push on that. Let's rule out the red flags. Have you noticed any black stools?
No.
Any unexplained weight loss in the last few months?
No. If anything, I'm up a bit.
Good. How about your bowels in general, any trouble there?
They're fine.
And your breathing, any trouble with that?
Nothing. Normal.
Any medical conditions I should know about?
Anxiety. For a few years now.
Okay, thanks for telling me. Any stomach problems in the family?
My father had stomach ulcers. Years ago.
Noted. Do you smoke?
Never smoked.
And alcohol?
A beer on weekends. Two at most.
That's modest. Let's get your numbers. Sleeve up, please.
Blood pressure is 118/76. Heart rate 68.
Okay.
Temperature is 36.8 °C. Breathing rate is 14 a minute.
Is that normal?
Perfectly. Oxygen saturation is 98%. And you're 71 kg on the scale.
Sounds right.
Everything on the list looks solid. So here's where I come out. Your stomach complaint started around the time something changed in your routine, and that's a useful clue.
You think it's connected?
It may be. I'm not going to say more than that from a chat and a set of vitals.
Fine.
Options, then. One: give it a couple more weeks, since new things often settle. Two: change when you take it, say with food instead of before.
Which should I do?
Try the timing change first. It costs nothing and it's low risk.
Okay.
Three: if neither helps, speak to whoever prescribed it before you change anything. Don't stop it on your own.
I wasn't going to.
Good. Also, keep the weekend beer in check until this settles. Alcohol irritates the stomach.
Easy enough.
And smaller meals help too. Big dinners late at night tend to make things worse.
Got it.
Also, water between meals rather than a big glass with food. It sounds minor, but it adds up when your stomach is touchy.
Okay, I can do that.
Any questions for me?
Do I need to come back?
Not unless it gets worse. If you see blood, or you can't keep food down, come in right away. Otherwise, you're good.
Understood.
That's all from me. Check out at the front desk.
Thanks, doctor.

clinical_actions.description: Try taking it with food, give it a couple of weeks, cut alcohol and eat smaller meals; speak to prescriber before changing anything
